title: Learning strategy under acquisition shift
formal_question: Does a source-only acquisition-aware deep representation improve station-supported chemical identification for an unseen instrument and unseen physical masters over a rigorously selected classical pipeline?
primary_comparison: frozen acquisition-aware deep minus development-selected classical under PP-U-MIN
success_interpretation: G4 supports a deep methods claim with its measured scope
failure_interpretation: G4 failure routes to a classical benchmark or instability study

title: Universal preprocessing sensitivity
formal_question: How do one universal smoothing or baseline-correction rule change transfer and model ranking relative to minimal min-max?
primary_comparison: paired PP-U-SG and PP-U-ARPLS minus PP-U-MIN within each frozen model
selection_boundary: identical source-only split and tuning procedure for every policy
success_interpretation: A consistent paired gain identifies a useful universal policy for this population
failure_interpretation: A loss or model-dependent effect supports retaining minimal preprocessing and reporting heterogeneity
prohibited_claim: clean-spectrum recovery or universal background-removal superiority

title: Platform-family-aware preprocessing
formal_question: For a held acquisition unit from a represented platform family does a source-selected family action improve transfer over universal minimal preprocessing?
primary_comparison: PP-FAMILY-SRC minus PP-U-MIN on identical domains with fallback-inclusive and supported-family estimands
population: 598-row primary with known-family eligible domains and all-domain fallback analysis
selection_boundary: source leave-one-unit-out pseudo-domains and metadata-only support rule
success_interpretation: Gain with adequate coverage supports family-conditioned preprocessing for represented platform families
failure_interpretation: No gain or low coverage favors universal or QC-adaptive preprocessing
prohibited_claim: arbitrary per-instrument tuning or claims for unseen platform families

title: Identity-blind QC-adaptive preprocessing
formal_question: Can a source-frozen row-local QC gate choose minimal smoothing or baseline correction for a held instrument without its identity family or target-population statistics?
primary_comparison: PP-QC-SRC minus PP-U-MIN on identical rows and domains
selection_boundary: finite gate library selected on source pseudo-instrument domains
success_interpretation: A robust paired gain with stable actions supports identity-blind QC routing within the observed shift envelope
failure_interpretation: No gain instability or heavy fallback favors universal preprocessing and identifies inadequate QC features
prohibited_claim: generalization to every new instrument or evidence of denoising

title: Value of target-instrument access
formal_question: How much do disjoint unlabeled paired or labelled target calibration masters change performance beyond frozen zero-shot pipelines?
primary_comparison: UDA paired-calibration and few-shot learning curves versus their zero-shot baseline
information_regime: unlabeled target adaptation versus paired calibration versus supervised few-shot
selection_boundary: calibration or adaptation masters disjoint from evaluation masters
success_interpretation: Learning curves quantify the value and type of target information
failure_interpretation: No gain shows that the registered target access is insufficient or unstable

title: Calibrated robustness and selective operation
formal_question: How stable are frozen pipelines to plausible spectral perturbations quality tiers and abstention?
primary_comparison: degradation and risk-coverage relative to each unperturbed frozen pipeline
selection_boundary: primary conclusions frozen before robustness inspection
success_interpretation: Small degradation and useful calibrated coverage support bounded operational robustness
failure_interpretation: Large or heterogeneous degradation identifies unsafe conditions and limits claims
prohibited_claim: claiming simulated perturbations reproduce a specific physical instrument

title: Narrow unknown-chemical rejection
formal_question: Can frozen station-conditioned models reject one held nonblank chemical while retaining known-class performance?
primary_comparison: frozen classical and deep known-only scores across eight held station-chemical tasks
population: 598-row station subsets with one held chemical
independent_unit: held station-chemical task and physical master
selection_boundary: held unknown absent from fitting score selection calibration and thresholds
success_interpretation: Consistent task-level rejection supports only the declared narrow stress-test claim
failure_interpretation: Failure demonstrates open-set fragility and cannot alter the primary route
prohibited_claim: general open-world or arbitrary unseen-chemical identification

title: Representation mechanism and failure structure
formal_question: Do acquisition-aware objectives change cross-view consistency and residual domain information while retaining chemistry?
primary_comparison: frozen embedding probes paired-view diagnostics and attribution controls across D0 and the selected acquisition-aware model
population: primary predictions embeddings and same-master pairs
information_regime: frozen source-only models with training-only probes
selection_boundary: no probe or attribution result selects a model
success_interpretation: Joint chemistry retention transfer gain and lower adjusted domain increment support a bounded invariance interpretation
failure_interpretation: Reduced domain predictability without retained chemistry is collapse rather than useful invariance
prohibited_claim: causal chemical-nuisance disentanglement or bond assignment without references
